Reconstructed saved frontier matches 10,000 subsequent allocations.
Low-half overflow carries into high half, including contiguous authored exclusions across carry.
Last usable identity exhausts the frontier without wrapping; exclusion-only exhaustion leaves failed allocation state unchanged.

limitations: Internal prerequisite only: public runtime spawn/despawn is not exposed.
Runtime snapshots do not yet persist the public allocator cursor or changed membership. Cursor reconstruction is a standalone helper test, not end-to-end lifecycle save qualification.
The owner must validate restored live IDs and provenance against the saved frontier and complete original authored exclusions, including deleted authored IDs.
Rollback may restore allocation state only together with the complete failed transaction; tentative IDs must not escape publication.
No Windows execution qualification, desktop package, or performance claim for this source state.
